Riegos Salz · Automatic Synchronization with Odoo

This system allows connecting Odoo with the Riegos Salz platform to automatically import historical data from sensors (flow, pressure, etc.) installed in the remote control system.

Once configured, the system automatically retrieves the values recorded in the Riegos Salz cloud and stores them in Odoo as readings linked to their corresponding sensors. This makes all irrigation system information available inside Odoo, simplifying analysis, comparison, and monitoring of the measured variables.

1) Connection setup

In the remote control configuration tab, fill in the Connection Parameters section with the username and password used in Riegos Salz.

{
  "username": "USERNAME",
  "password": "PASSWORD"
}

The system uses these credentials to connect with the Riegos Salz web service. During the process, the password is automatically encrypted internally (MD5 format), ensuring that it is never sent in plain text.

The connection is made through the secure Riegos Salz web service (https://cloudcontrol.riegosalz.com/wm-rest.php), which accepts requests in JSON format.

2) Configure devices and sensors

Devices

Each device must define a start date from which historical data should be retrieved. This date is placed in the device's Remote Control Parameters field:

{
  "start_date": "2025-10-01"
}

If no date is specified, the system will use January 1st of the current year by default. The start date limits the range of queries and helps optimize download time.

Sensors

Each sensor must have a linked variable ID from Riegos Salz. This number uniquely identifies the measurement point (for example, a flow meter or pressure sensor) in the Riegos Salz platform.

In the sensor's Remote Control Parameters field, enter:

{
  "id": 42955
}

If a sensor does not have this number, it cannot be synchronized.

The variable IDs can be obtained from the Riegos Salz platform or through the system's technical equipment list.

Depending on the installation, the identification number (id) may correspond to different types of measurements, for example:

  • LEVEL
  • FLOW
  • VELOCITY
  • OPENING

3) Running the process

1. Get sensor plan

The “Get devices (plan)” action scans all configured sensors and internally generates a list containing the sensors, their devices, their Riegos Salz IDs, and the start date from which readings should be downloaded.

This step does not download data yet; it only prepares the synchronization plan.

2. Download readings

The “Get readings” action contacts Riegos Salz and retrieves the historical data for each sensor included in the plan.

Each reading includes a value and a timestamp, for example: Flow = 35 l/s on 10/10/2025 at 10:00.

The system automatically saves each reading in Odoo, under the corresponding sensor record. This way, daily historical data is continuously stored for later viewing and analysis.

The process uses the consultaHistoricos command from the Riegos Salz API. Communication is done in JSON format, with the following main fields:

{
  "comando": "consultaHistoricos",
  "correo": "USERNAME",
  "contrasenya": "PASSWORD",
  "variables": [42955],
  "fechaIni": "2025-10-01 00:00:00"
}

The API returns a list of readings, each containing two values: the timestamp (for example, "2025-10-15 08:00:00") and the measured value (for example, "75"). Each pair becomes a reading in Odoo.

The system performs one request per configured sensor, ensuring that each reading is linked to the correct sensor and device.

4) Results and reports

Once synchronization is completed:

  • A message appears in the remote control record showing the total number of readings created and any detected errors.
  • A JSON file (.json) is generated with a detailed summary of the operation: processed sensors, dates, total readings, and any errors.

This file can be viewed in the remote control attachments section in Odoo. A summary message is also recorded in the same entry, allowing historical tracking of past synchronizations.

5) Tips and best practices

  • Verify that the Riegos Salz username and password are correct. If the password changes, update it in Odoo as well.
  • Ensure that each sensor has its variable ID correctly configured (the exact number provided by Riegos Salz).
  • The start date should match the first date you wish to retrieve data from. Setting it too far in the past may increase processing time.
  • Review the audit file after each execution to confirm that all readings were imported successfully.
  • If no data is returned, check in the Riegos Salz platform that the sensor has historical data for the indicated date range.
  • The Riegos Salz API updates its readings approximately every 15 minutes. It is recommended to schedule the synchronization in Odoo as a daily task to keep data up to date.

6) Full configuration example

Connection parameters in remote control:

{
  "username": "USERNAME",
  "password": "PASSWORD"
}

Device:

{
  "start_date": "2025-10-01"
}

Sensor:

{
  "id": 42955
}

Once configured, simply run the “Riegos Salz: Daily Sync” procedure so Odoo automatically connects, downloads the data, and stores it in the corresponding sensors.

The procedure can be run manually or scheduled as a recurring automatic task (cron) to execute daily without user intervention.

7) Common error messages

  • “Missing credentials”: the username or password is missing in the configuration.
  • “Invalid ID”: the sensor does not have a valid variable ID in Riegos Salz.
  • “No data found”: no readings are available on the platform for the specified date range.
  • “Timeout”: the connection took too long. Try running the action again later.
  • “Error 15”: the platform was temporarily unable to access historical data. Try again later.
  • “CodError ≠ 0”: the API returned an error code different from 0 (see official documentation for details).
